name: OWASP NodeGoat
intendedUse: Deliberately vulnerable Node.js app for learning and exploiting the OWASP Top 10; stated in the README: https://github.com/OWASP/NodeGoat/blob/9e35cae25f5c6226c30c7d9b03987005affb2888/README.md

image.note: No official image; built locally from the pinned commit's Dockerfile and docker-compose.yml (web + mongo). Base image digest to be pinned by the runner.

baseImages.note: Tag still on Docker Hub (inactive, single-arch legacy manifest, no index digest).
Tag still on Docker Hub (single-arch legacy manifest, no index digest).
Floating tag; digest as of 2026-10-22, will drift. Compose also needs config db pointed at mongo:27017 per README.

answerKey.title: NodeGoat tutorial (served at /tutorial): OWASP Top 10 2013 A1-A10, ReDoS, SSRF

builtBy: Claude (AI-assisted), from the NodeGoat tutorial pages and README at the pinned commit plus route/config source review; to be checked by labeller A

vulnerabilities.title: A1-1 Server Side JS Injection
vulnerabilities.description: Contribution form values are passed straight to eval(), letting a user run arbitrary JavaScript on the server.

vulnerabilities.title: A1-1 Server Side JS Injection (HTTP)
vulnerabilities.description: Same eval flaw exploited over HTTP by POSTing JavaScript in preTax/afterTax/roth while logged in.
vulnerabilities.note: Server-side JS injection is not one of the claimed probe types (SQLi/XSS/SSTI/cmdi/SSRF/redirect); authenticated POST body.

vulnerabilities.title: A1-2 NoSQL Injection ($where)
vulnerabilities.description: Allocations threshold is concatenated into a MongoDB $where expression, enabling JS injection and DoS.

vulnerabilities.title: A1-3 Log Injection
vulnerabilities.description: Failed-login username is logged unsanitised, so CRLF input can forge log lines.

vulnerabilities.title: A2-1 Protecting user credentials
vulnerabilities.description: User passwords are stored in the database in plain text instead of a salted hash.
vulnerabilities.appCategory: A2 Broken Authentication and Session Management
vulnerabilities.note: Weak/absent password hashing is not a claimed class.

vulnerabilities.title: A2-1 Session timeout and protecting cookies in transit
vulnerabilities.description: Session cookie lacks the Secure flag and any expiry; sessions never time out.
vulnerabilities.appCategory: A2 Broken Authentication and Session Management
vulnerabilities.note: Cookie is set on any first response (saveUninitialized). express-session sets HttpOnly by default, so only Secure/expiry are missing; app is plain HTTP.

vulnerabilities.title: A2-1 Session hijacking
vulnerabilities.description: Session id is not regenerated on login, so a pre-login session id stays valid afterwards.
vulnerabilities.appCategory: A2 Broken Authentication and Session Management
vulnerabilities.note: Session fixation is not among the claimed auth checks.

vulnerabilities.title: A2-2 Password Guessing Attacks
vulnerabilities.description: Login has no lockout or rate limiting, so passwords can be brute forced.
vulnerabilities.appCategory: A2 Broken Authentication and Session Management

vulnerabilities.title: A2-2 Weak password policy
vulnerabilities.description: Signup accepts any 1-20 character password; no length or complexity requirement.
vulnerabilities.appCategory: A2 Broken Authentication and Session Management

vulnerabilities.title: A2-2 Username/Password Enumeration
vulnerabilities.description: Login error says whether the username or the password was wrong, aiding enumeration.
vulnerabilities.appCategory: A2 Broken Authentication and Session Management
vulnerabilities.note: Username enumeration is not among the claimed auth checks.

vulnerabilities.title: A3 Cross-Site Scripting (stored, profile)
vulnerabilities.description: Profile first/last name are saved and echoed unescaped because template autoescape is disabled.
vulnerabilities.note: Swig autoescape:false in server.js is the root cause; not an innerHTML-style sink.

vulnerabilities.title: A3 Output Encoding Context
vulnerabilities.description: Profile value is HTML-encoded but placed in a different context, so encoding does not prevent XSS.

vulnerabilities.title: A4 Insecure Direct Object References
vulnerabilities.description: Allocations are fetched by the numeric user id in the URL without checking it is the logged-in user.

vulnerabilities.title: A5 X-Powered-By header
vulnerabilities.description: Express default X-Powered-By header is left on, disclosing the framework.

vulnerabilities.title: A5 Missing security headers (helmet disabled)
vulnerabilities.description: No X-Frame-Options, CSP, HSTS, nosniff or no-cache headers; helmet middleware is commented out.

vulnerabilities.title: A5 Default session cookie name
vulnerabilities.description: Session cookie keeps the default express name, revealing the stack.
vulnerabilities.note: Cookie-name fingerprinting is not a claimed cookie check (flags only).

vulnerabilities.title: A5 Outdated Node.js runtime
vulnerabilities.description: Container is built on end-of-life Node.js 4 images with public advisories.
vulnerabilities.note: Tutorial advises using the latest Node; the concrete location (FROM node:4.4 / node:4-alpine) comes from the Dockerfile.

vulnerabilities.title: A6 Sensitive Data Exposure: plain HTTP
vulnerabilities.description: App, including login and session cookie, is served only over unencrypted HTTP.
vulnerabilities.note: Only detectable if the scanner reports a plain-HTTP target as missing TLS.

vulnerabilities.title: A6 Sensitive data stored unencrypted
vulnerabilities.description: SSN and date of birth are stored in the database in plain text.

vulnerabilities.title: A7 Missing Function Level Access Control
vulnerabilities.description: Admin-only benefits page is reachable by any logged-in user; route lacks an admin check.
vulnerabilities.appCategory: A7 Missing Function Level Access Control

vulnerabilities.title: A8 Cross-Site Request Forgery
vulnerabilities.description: State-changing forms such as profile update carry no CSRF token; csurf is commented out.

vulnerabilities.title: A9 Insecure dependency: Marked
vulnerabilities.description: Old Marked markdown library renders memos server-side and lets javascript: links through (XSS).
vulnerabilities.appCategory: A9 Using Components with Known Vulnerabilities
vulnerabilities.note: Server-side npm dependency (marked 0.3.9), not served to the browser; exploitation is also stored XSS.

vulnerabilities.title: A10 Unvalidated Redirects and Forwards
vulnerabilities.description: /learn redirects to whatever URL is in the url query parameter.
vulnerabilities.note: Route is behind isLoggedIn; unauthenticated requests redirect to /login.

vulnerabilities.title: ReDoS Regular Expressions DoS
vulnerabilities.description: Bank routing number is checked with a catastrophically backtracking regex, blocking the event loop.

vulnerabilities.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
vulnerabilities.description: Research page fetches url+symbol query parameters server-side and returns the response body.
vulnerabilities.note: Fetched body is reflected, so in-band detection is possible without an external server.

vulnerabilities.title: Hardcoded session cookie secret
vulnerabilities.description: Session signing secret is a hardcoded literal in the default config file.
vulnerabilities.note: Not a tutorial item; added from source review. Tutorial A5 references config.cookieSecret. Value looks like a placeholder. Found in source, not in the tutorial; kept for labelling (a finding here can be correct) but not in the recall denominator.

vulnerabilities.title: Hardcoded crypto key
vulnerabilities.description: Data encryption key is a hardcoded literal in the default config file.
vulnerabilities.note: Not a tutorial item; added from source review (A6 fix uses config.cryptoKey). Value looks like a placeholder. Found in source, not in the tutorial; kept for labelling (a finding here can be correct) but not in the recall denominator.

vulnerabilities.title: MongoDB connection string with credentials
vulnerabilities.description: Default database URL embeds a username and password for a hosted MongoDB instance.
vulnerabilities.note: Not a tutorial item; added from source review. README points to this config file. Found in source, not in the tutorial; kept for labelling (a finding here can be correct) but not in the recall denominator.

vulnerabilities.title: Hardcoded ZAP API key
vulnerabilities.description: OWASP ZAP API key for security regression tests is hardcoded in two env config files.
vulnerabilities.note: Not a tutorial item; added from source review. Test-tooling key, not an app credential. Found in source, not in the tutorial; kept for labelling (a finding here can be correct) but not in the recall denominator.

vulnerabilities.title: Committed TLS private key
vulnerabilities.description: RSA private key for the HTTPS fix is committed to the repository.
vulnerabilities.note: Not described as a vuln in the tutorial; key file is referenced by the commented A6 fix in server.js. Found in source, not in the tutorial; kept for labelling (a finding here can be correct) but not in the recall denominator.

vulnerabilities.title: Default user accounts
vulnerabilities.description: Database seed creates admin and user accounts with published passwords.
